items.text: On Thursday, Russian forces started an invasion of Ukraine. The Russian president Vladimir Putin announced a special military operation; however, world leaders warned him that it could spark the biggest war in Europe since 1945. A series of air strikes hit airports across the country, and on Friday, the highways leaving the capital city of Kyiv were jammed as people tried to leave. Hundreds of thousand of refugees have fled Ukraine to neighboring countries, around half of which have traveled to the Polish border. On Ukraine-Slovakia border, volunteers are helping arrange food, clothing, transportation and accommodation for new arrivals, with the UN refugee agency warning that as many as 5 million Ukrainians could leave the country. Meanwhile, the US, Canada and key European countries have agreed to remove selected Russian banks from the Swift international payments system, and the EU has imposed economic sanctions on Russia. In response, Putin has ordered his military to put the country’s nuclear forces on high alert . Difficult words: invasion (when an army or country enters and takes control of another country by force), sanction (a strong action taken in order to make someone obey a law or rule, or a punishment given when they don’t obey), alert (the state of being watchful and ready). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On Thursday, Russian soldiers attacked Ukraine. World leaders strongly criticized the attack, and they said that it could start a big war in Europe. Russian rockets hit several airports and cities, and soldiers were getting closer to the capital city of Kyiv. Hundreds of thousands of people left Ukraine, and they traveled mainly to the Polish and Slovak border. The UN said that 5 million Ukrainians could leave the country because of the war. Western countries imposed strict sanctions on Russia, and they agreed to cut some Russian banks off from the international payment system. As a reaction, the Russian president Vladimir Putin put Russian nuclear forces on high alert . Difficult words: The UN (The United Nations, an organization which tries to keep peace in the world), sanction (a strong action which a country or organization takes against another country to make it follow rules), alert (when someone is careful and ready to do something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On Thursday, Russian soldiers attack Ukraine. World leaders don’t agree with the attack. They say that a war can start in Europe. Russia attacks Ukrainian airports and big cities. Hundreds of thousands of people leave Ukraine. They are scared. They travel mainly to Poland and Slovakia. They get clothes and food there. Some people say that 5 million Ukrainians will leave the country. Western countries must stop Russia. They impose sanctions on Russia. Sanctions hit Russia’s business. Some Russian banks can’t use international payment system. Planes don’t fly to and from Russia. The Russian president Vladimir Putin says that he is ready to use nuclear rockets . Difficult words: airport (a place where planes take off and land), impose (to make something a rule by force), nuclear rocket (a rocket which is very dangerous, and it can kill many people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Danish brewer Carlsberg said it would raise beer prices this year to offset the rising costs of ingredients and transportation. Prices of raw materials have risen across the world for many industries. Supply struggled to keep up with demand as countries recovered from the pandemic last year. Overall costs per liter of beer increased as much as 12%, and Carlsberg acknowledged higher prices could negatively impact customers. In 2021, Carlsberg’s net profit increased by 13% despite bars and restaurants closing some of its markets. This year, the company expects the net profit to increase again. Carlsberg is now looking at more markets to focus on ciders, seltzers , alcohol-free beverages, and premium brands. Difficult words: offset (to reduce the effect of something), net profit (the profit after subtracting all costs, taxes, and interests), seltzer (mineral water with bubbles). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Carlsberg is a Danish company that makes beer. Last week, it announced that it would raise the prices of its products. The cost of one liter of beer went up by 12% last year because the costs of ingredients and transportation went up. When businesses started to improve after the coronavirus, companies had problems producing enough raw materials. Raw materials are the things that people use to make other things. As a result, the prices of materials went up a lot. Carlsberg said that higher prices may mean that people will drink less beer. Now the company wants to sell more of its other products, for example, ciders , mineral water, and alcohol-free beer. Difficult words: raise (to make something higher), ingredient (one of all the different things which are a part of a drink or food), cider (an alcoholic drink from apple juice). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Carlsberg is a Danish company. It makes beer. It is the third biggest brewer in the world. Carlsberg says that its beer will cost more. The prices of ingredients cost more. Transportation costs more. Transportation is when you move things to other places. Many things cost more after COVID-19. It is because companies cannot make enough materials. Materials are the things you use to make other things. Many businesses are open again. Some people may drink less beer. Carlsberg plans to sell more of its other drinks. These drinks are ciders , mineral water, and alcohol-free beer. Difficult words: brewer (a company which makes beer), ingredient (one of all the different things in a drink or food), cider (an alcoholic drink from apple juice). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In 2021, at least 688 Americans died from weather events, mostly due to February’s southern winter storm and extreme heat in the Pacific Northwest. Experts say climate change mostly causes these events. Homeless people have no protection from extreme weather, and this negatively impacts their life expectancy and quality of life. However, as the homeless suffer from climate change, it also creates homelessness. Extreme weather events displace 20 million people worldwide from their homes every year. Until the climate crisis gets solved, governments need to offer more affordable housing options. However, people who run shelters say it is difficult to make a homeless person move into a regular home. Homeless people are often used to living in communities, and the first step to help them is to build trust between them and local area shelters. Building trust can be a lengthy process. Difficult words: life expectancy (the length of time a living thing is likely to live), displace (to force someone to leave home, usually because of war or natural disaster), lengthy (taking or continuing for a long time). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Reports say that in 2021, almost 700 Americans died because of bad weather. Last year, there were winter storms as well as heatwaves , and they made the lives of homeless people harder. Experts believe that climate change is the main reason for extreme weather. Homeless people do not have a place to stay when it is either too hot or too cold. Local shelters and churches help homeless people, but it is difficult. These people only know life on the street, and they want to be with other homeless people. Sometimes they do not want to stay in apartments where they are alone or places where they have man rules. Climate change also makes more people homeless. Experts say that 20 million people worldwide must leave their homes every year because of floods, fires, or storms. Difficult words: heatwave (a time when the weather is much hotter than usual), homeless (without a home), extreme (very unusual), shelter (a safe place where people can stay). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Thousands of people die because of bad weather every year. Almost 700 Americans die last year. Homeless people are people without a home. They live in the street. They stay outside when it is very hot. They do not have enough water. Sometimes it is too cold. They need more clothes and blankets . Homeless people can sometimes stay in shelters and churches. They do not know how to live differently. They sometimes do not want any help. Unusual weather makes more people homeless. 20 million people must leave their homes every year. There are more floods , fires, or storms. It is very difficult to solve the problem. Unusual weather happens more and more often. Difficult words: blanket (a large piece of cloth which keeps someone warm), shelter (a safe place), flood (when it rains too much, and water is in houses and streets). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A fire engulfed a ferry on Friday as it sailed from Greece to Italy. 239 passengers and 51 crew members were on board the ferry when the fire started. Rescue vessels took most of the people to the Greek island of Corfu where ambulances were already waiting. Meanwhile, firefighters were still battling to rescue people who were trapped in the ship’s garage, and eight people were missing. The ferry carried 153 vehicles, and many of them were trucks. One of the drivers said that the cars had been the worst thing, because they were standing too close next to each other, and there was no escape route. Witnesses said that the flames were very high, and they could see them from many kilometers away. According to the passengers, the fire was so big and wide that it became unmanageable quickly. Difficult words: engulf (to surround), trap (to stop someone from escaping), unmanageable (difficult or impossible to handle or control). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A fire started on an Italian ferry on Friday night. The ferry sailed from Greece to Italy, and there were 290 people on board . Witnesses said that the fire probably started in one of the holds . The fire spread so quickly that it was impossible to stop it. There were 153 vehicles on board, and many of them were trucks. One driver said that the trucks stood so close to each other that it was impossible to escape. Rescue boats took most of the people to the Greek island of Corfu, and 10 people ended up in hospital. Rescuers were still looking for eight people. Difficult words: ferry (a boat which moves people and vehicles), onboard (on a ship, plane, or another vehicle), hold (the part of a ship to keep things and move them to another place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A ferry is a ship. It usually takes people, things, and cars across a river or the sea. It is Friday night. An Italian ferry is traveling from Greece to Italy. 290 people are on the ship. Most of them are from Bulgaria, Turkey, and Romania. A fire starts. It spreads very quickly. People run away. 153 cars and trucks are on the ship. They stand very close to each other. People can’t pass through . Rescuers take most of the people to a safe place. 10 people must go to the hospital. Rescuers are still looking for eight people. Nobody knows where they are. Difficult words: spread (to move around a place or area), pass through (to move through a place on the way to another place), look for (to try to find something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A strain of influenza has spread in Kentucky and Virginia, US; it is deadly to chickens and other fowl . Farms hope they’ll avoid an outbreak similar to the one in 2015 that killed 50 million birds across 15 US states. The virus was spreading for months in Europe and Asia, and people found it in wild birds in Canada before health officials found an outbreak at a turkey farm in Indiana, US. Wild birds often carry strains of influenza; however, they usually don’t get sick. Those strains get easily into farm birds, and they mutate into more deadly viruses. If the virus spreads more, egg, turkey, and chicken prices will likely rise, and the availability of these products will drop. Mexico is among the countries that already banned or limited poultry purchases from Indiana after officials found the virus there. Difficult words: strain of influenza (a variety of a common sickness), fowl (a bird that people eat as food, for example, a hen or duck), mutate (to develop a new form). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In recent months, there were many cases of bird flu in Europe and Asia. Now, it has spread to the US, too. Health officials found the flu at a turkey farm in Indiana, and some countries have already stopped buying poultry from the state. The flu spread also to Kentucky and Virginia, where farmers tried to stop it. They were afraid that the situation could be as bad as in 2015. That year, bird flu killed 50 million birds in 15 US states. Migratory birds often spread the disease which causes bird flu, but the flu isn’t very dangerous for them. When the flu gets to domestic birds, it changes and is very dangerous. Difficult words: poultry (the meat of chickens, turkeys, and other birds), migratory (an animal which travels from one place to another, usually because of weather), domestic (an animal which people keep at home or on a farm). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Bird flu is a disease. It kills birds. It is not very dangerous for wild birds. It is very dangerous for domestic birds. Domestic birds live on farms. For example, they are chickens, turkeys, or ducks. Bird flu is in Europe and Asia some months ago. It spreads to the US. Officials first know about bird flu in Indiana. It spreads to Kentucky and Virginia. Farmers worry. They remember bird flu in 2015. It kills 50 million birds in 15 US states. Some countries already don’t want meat from Indiana. Farmers must solve the problem quickly. Prices of poultry will probably get higher. Difficult words: wild (an animal which lives freely and not on a farm), spread (to move around an area), poultry (the meat of chickens, turkeys, and other birds). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A long-time lover of creepy crawlies , a 32-year-old Chinese man got the idea for a cockroach farm after a friend who worked in a pharmacy told him about the use of bugs as a cheap source of protein and medication. The man gave up his job and moved to the country to live among the bugs. The cockroaches sell for $16 a kilo, which does not sound like a lot, but brings the farmer a fortune from his crop. Cockroach shells and oils are used in Chinese medicine to treat everything from heart disease to hepatitis and burns. Unsurprisingly, however, many people are not so keen on smearing themselves in cockroach oil, so it is not usually marketed as what it really is. Difficult words: creepy (making you feel unwell), crawly (something which moves on four legs with its body close to the ground), hepatitis (a sickness when there’s something wrong with the liver), smear (cover). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Most people don’t like cockroaches, but one man from China is an exception . He has a cockroach farm which brings him a fortune . He has nearly one square mile of the bugs, and one kilo of them sells for $16. People use cockroach shells and oil in Chinese medicine to treat a lot of diseases. However, these medical products say nothing about the cockroaches on their information packets . The reason why is clear. But, the farmer is proud of his cockroach farm anyway. Difficult words: exception (he is different, not like most people), fortune (a lot of money), packet (box in which the medicine is). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Do you like cockroaches? Well, most people don’t. However, one man from China loves them. He has a cockroach farm. He has around one mile square of cockroaches. One kilo of cockroaches sells for $16. The farm brings the man a lot of money. People use cockroach shells and oil in Chinese medicine. They treat a lot of diseases . Difficult words: shell (hard outer part of the bug’s body), treat (make the disease less serious/help the ill person), disease (something which makes you feel unwell). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Coca-Cola said that it’ll aim for 25% of its global packaging to be reusable and to recycle all packaging by 2030. In the past, environmental groups criticized Coca-Cola for worldwide plastic pollution, and they praised the company’s move. The company was the world’s worst plastic polluter for the fourth year in a row in 2021, and only 16% of its packaging was reusable in 2020. Coca-Cola acknowledged that food and drink companies were responsible for much of the litter on streets, beaches, and in the oceans worldwide. The company also said that it followed the idea of a circular economy where resources such as aluminum, plastic, and glass are reused rather than thrown away. However, critics said that the company should focus on reducing instead of recycling waste. Difficult words: praise (to express respect or approval of what someone did), acknowledge (to admit that something’s true), circular economy (a system in which raw materials, components, and products lose little value). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Coca-Cola is a company that makes soft drinks, and it is also the world’s worst plastic polluter . Many people and companies criticized Coca-Cola that it did nothing to limit its plastic. The company officially said that it knew about the problem with plastic on streets, beaches, and in the oceans. It finally promised to do something with it. Coca-Cola said that it would be possible to recycle all its packaging by 2030. Also, 25% of the packaging will be reusable. It means that people will be able to use something more than once. Not everyone was happy about the news. Some people said that reducing trash was more important than recycling. Difficult words: polluter (a person or company which puts bad things in the water, air, and so on), limit (to use less), recycle (to use things and materials to make new things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Coca-Cola is an American company. It makes soft drinks . It makes more than 500 different drinks. Most drinks come in plastic. Cans are from aluminum. People throw bottles and cans away. Many end up on streets, beaches, and in the ocean. Coca-Cola hurts the natural world a lot. The company officially says that it is true. It is time to change it now. The company will recycle all its plastic by 2030. Many people and companies are happy. Some say that it is not enough. It is more important to reduce plastic and not recycle it. Difficult words: soft drink (a non-alcoholic drink such as lemonade or fruit juice), recycle (to use materials and old things for making new things), reduce (to make something smaller). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The tradition for heterosexual couples in the US is women take their husbands’ last names after they get married. However, nontraditional decisions are happening more often. In many cultures around the world, women typically add their husbands’ last names to their own. According to a 2019 survey, just 3% of American men changed to their wives’ last names, and that’s why there’s no male equivalent for the term ‘ maiden name ’. In the US, some couples do a combination of their last names. They like the idea of individual and family identities and how to combine the two. However, they still respect the family name to publish professionally. In the 2010s, around 22% of married women kept their last name after they got married, and most of them were highly educated, high-earning, and established in their careers. Difficult words: heterosexual (a person who’s sexually attracted to people of the opposite sex), equivalent (a thing that’s the same or equal to something else), maiden name (the original last name of a married woman, who uses her husband’s last name after their marriage). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In many countries in the world, women usually take their husbands’ last names after they get married. In other countries, women usually keep their own last names, and they add their husbands’, too. Men do not usually take their wives’ last names. In the US, only about 3% of men do it. There is no similar term for ‘ maiden name’ for men. The maiden name is the last name of a woman before she got married, and then she took her husband’s name. In the US, it is happening more and more often that couples use a combination of their last names. For example, they make a word that starts with the first letters of the husband’s last name, and it ends with the woman’s first letters of her last name. It is unusual, and a court must approve the new last name. Difficult words: maiden (a girl or young woman who is not married), combination (a mixture of two or more things together), approve (to officially agree with something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Many women change their last names when they get married. Women in many countries use their husbands’ last names. Some women use both last names. Not many men change their last names when they get married. Only about 3% of American men do it. More and more couples do something different. They use a new last name. They often put together their last names. They make one last name from them. This is not usual. A court must officially agree with the new name. Some women keep their last name. They have a good job. Many people know them. They don’t want to change who they are. Difficult words: last name (the person’s family name which comes after the first name), couple (two people or things that are together), court (a group of people who officially decide about official things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A college student named Muskan Khan became a symbol of resistance in India’s Karnataka state, where tensions are rising over the right to wear religious clothing to school. Khan attempted to hand in a college assignment when a group of men approached and stopped her because she was wearing a burqa . The woman had covered her head with a hijab, an Islamic headscarf, and the men demanded that she take it off. In another state school, a group of girls could not enter the classroom because the girls wore hijabs. Activists say that these events are part of a crackdown on India’s minority Muslim population, and the crackdown started when Prime Minister Narendra Modi came to power nearly eight years ago. They say that the government is denying religious freedom enshrined in Indian laws. After a week of protests, some schools in Karnataka reopened; however, the state’s education minister said that he supported banning the hijab in educational institutions. Difficult words: burqa (a piece of clothing that covers the whole head and body, and some Muslim women wear it), crackdown (a strong official action to punish people who break laws), enshrined (protected or preserved). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Eight years ago, the government in India changed, and since that time, some Muslim women had problems in schools. Some Muslim students wore the burqa, which is a special piece of clothing that covers the whole body and head. Others wore a headscarf called a hijab. This was a problem for many people who didn’t like religious clothing. 10% of people in India are Muslims, and Muslim women said that it was their right to wear the hijab and burqa. The government in the Karnataka state banned the hijab in state schools, but after a week of protests, Muslim women could return to schools. Difficult words: religious (related to a god), right (something that people can legally or officially have or do), ban (to stop something officially). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The hijab is a piece of clothing. It covers the whole body and head. Some Muslim women wear it. Some Muslim women wear a burqa. A burqa is a headscarf . Some people are Muslims in India. The government changes some rules for Muslim people. Muslim students in India have problems in schools. The government in Karnataka state bans the hijab in state schools. Women can’t go to school when they wear it. Muslim women protest. They say that they can wear religious clothes. It is something that they can officially do. Muslim students return to school after one week. It is not the end. Officials say that they don’t want burqas and hijabs in schools. Difficult words: headscarf (a square piece of cloth which a woman wears on her head), ban (to officially stop something), religious (related to a god). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In the northern Mexican city of Cuauhtémoc, a security camera filmed hundred of yellow-headed blackbirds falling out of the sky. The birds fly to Mexico for winter. The footage showed a flock of birds falling onto houses like a cloud of black smoke. Most birds managed to fly off; however, later footage showed carcasses of the birds scattered on streets of the city. According to some reports, high levels of pollution could have been the reason for the incident. Another suggestion was the birds were electrocuted while they were resting on power lines. It was also possible that a predator made the birds swirl tightly and chased them to the ground to make a catch. However, the cause of the mysterious deaths remained unclear. Difficult words: carcass (the dead body of an animal), electrocute (to injure or kill someone by an electric shock), swirl (to move around in circles or spirals). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A security camera filmed a flock of birds falling from the sky. The event happened in the Mexican city of Cuauhtémoc. The birds looked like a black cloud that suddenly fell to the ground. Most birds flew away, but some of them stayed on the streets, and they died. Nobody really knows what happened to the animals. Some people said that dirty air could be the problem, while others suggested that power lines killed the birds. It is also possible that a predator tried to catch a bird, and the flock flew to the ground. The birds were yellow-headed blackbirds. They stay in the US and Canada in summer, and they migrate to Mexico for winter. Difficult words: flock (a group of animals, for example, birds, sheep, or goats), predator (an animal that kills another animal for food), migrate (to move from one area to another, usually because of the weather). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A security camera in a Mexican city films something unusual. Birds fall from the sky. The birds look like a black cloud. They fly to the ground. Most birds fly away. Some animals stay on the ground. They die. People have different opinions about the event. Some people say that dirty air is the problem. Others say that electricity kills the animals. Many people believe that there is a predator . The birds want to fly away from the predator. Then they are confused . They hit the ground. The birds are yellow-headed blackbirds. They stay in the US and Canada in the summer. They fly to Mexico for winter. It is warmer in Mexico. Difficult words: opinion (what a person thinks about something), predator (an animal which kills another animal, and it eats it), confused (when somebody can’t think clearly). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

15-year-old Russian figure skater Kamila Valieva tested positive for the banned drug trimetazidine before the Beijing 2022 Olympic Games; however, tests found the result after she helped Team Russia win the team figure skating competition. The Russian anti-doping agency temporarily suspended Valieva and then reinstated her on February 9. The Court of Arbitration for Sport will determine if Valieva can continue to compete in Beijing in other events. A lab took the sample on December 25 last year and then reported the results on February 8. Doctors typically use the drug to treat chest pain and dizziness; however, according to the International Testing Agency, it can boost endurance and blood flow. Valieva is the current world record holder, and she’s set nine world records in her career. The Olympic medal ceremony will wait until the court resolves the case. Difficult words: anti-doping agency (an organization that monitors banned drugs in sports), reinstate (to return someone in a job or position), endurance (the ability to do something for a long time). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Kamila Valieva is a 15-year-old Russian figure skater who is competing at the Winter Olympics in Beijing, China. In December last year, a lab took a sample of her blood to check if Valieva used illegal drugs. On February 8, the results came that Valieva used trimetazidine. Doctors normally give this drug to patients with heart problems. Since 2014, athletes can’t use this drug because it is possible to train harder and longer. Valieva and her team already won a gold medal at the Olympics, but officials postponed the medal ceremony . A court will decide if Valieva will be in other Olympic events. Difficult words: lab (a place where scientists work), sample (a small piece of something), medal ceremony (when the best athletes get medals at the end of a game or competition). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Kamila Valieva is a figure skater . She comes from Russia. She is 15 years old. She is at the Winter Olympic Games in China. Valieva and her team win a gold medal at the Games. Officials give them no medals. A Swedish lab checks Valieva’s blood in December. Valieva has an illegal drug in her blood. The name of the drug is trimetazidine. Athletes can’t use it since 2014. They train harder and longer with the drug. A court must decide what happens to Valieva. The court will say if Valieva can be in other Olympic events. Difficult words: figure skater (a person who moves quickly and jumps on ice), illegal (against the rules), drug (a medicine or thing which affects the body). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Someone shot a journalist in the southern state of Oaxaca on Thursday, the fifth killed in Mexico this year, and the third in two weeks. Officials confirmed that the victim was Heber López, the director of the online news site Noticias Web. Police held the two suspects in custody , and they recovered a gun from them. The two men walked into López’s recording studio, and they shot him. Reportedly, his 12-year-old son was there but uninjured. López covered crime and police news, and he regularly wrote about politics and corruption in the local government. López worked in the port city of Salina Cruz, and he received death threats in 2019. According to another journalist and López’s friends, he never told them about the threats. However, they believed the killing was a response to his work. According to a human rights organization called Article 19, people killed at least 145 journalists in Mexico from 2000 to 2021, which made the country one of the deadliest for journalists. Difficult words: custody (in prison), corruption (illegal or dishonest behavior by people who are in power), death threat (a threat to kill someone, often anonymous). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Heber López was a journalist, who worked in the city of Salina Cruz, Mexico. He often wrote about the crime and corruption of local politicians. In 2019, López got death threats. They were anonymous letters that said that someone would kill him. López tells no one about the letters. Last week, a white van stopped in front of López’s office. Two men came into the office and shot him. Reportedly, his 12-year-old son was with him, but he wasn’t hurt. Police arrested two men, and they found a gun. López was the fifth journalist in Mexico who died this year. Over 145 journalists died in Mexico from 2000 to 2021. It was one of the most dangerous countries for journalists. Difficult words: corruption (when politicians or other important people do something bad or illegal), anonymous (from or by a person whose name nobody knows), van (a big closed car which people usually use to carry things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Heber López comes from Mexico. He is a journalist . He works in the city of Salina Cruz. López writes about crime . He writes about problems in government. He gets letters in 2019. These letters say that somebody will kill him. López tells no one about the letters. A white car stops in front of the man’s office last week. Two men get out of the car. They have a gun. They kill López. Some people think that the man’s son is in the office, too. Nothing happens to him. Police arrest the men. They have a gun. Five journalists die in Mexico this year. Over 145 journalists die since 2000. Mexico is one of the most dangerous countries for journalists. Difficult words: journalist (a person who writes for newspapers or news websites), crime (when someone does something very bad, and he breaks the rules of a country), arrest (to go with the police because you do something bad). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A Black Hawk helicopter flew for the first time without pilots in Kentucky, US. The aircraft flew for 30 minutes with no passengers on Saturday and again on Monday. It flew through a simulated city space, avoided imagined buildings, and then, performed a perfect landing. The testing was a part of the so-called ALIAS program that promotes high-level automation . Engineers install autonomous technology into military aircraft, and it makes them fly with no pilot. According to the program manager, the technology reduces pilots’ workload, and they can focus on mission management instead of the mechanics. Pilots will operate aircraft at all times and in many conditions to achieve their missions. Difficult words: simulate (to make a computer model of something), automation (the use of machines or computers instead of people to do a job), autonomous (not controlled by others). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

For the first time, a military helicopter flew without pilots. There were two flights on Saturday and Monday, and they lasted about 30 minutes. There were no passengers on board. Engineers installed a special technology in the helicopter which made it possible to fly without pilots. The Black Hawk helicopter flew through a simulated city, and then it landed perfectly at Fort Campbell, US. This technology helps pilots to focus on missions instead of flying helicopters. They fly in many types of weather, at night, and when they can’t see very well. The military hopes that it will make missions more successful. Difficult words: military (connected to soldiers and army), simulated (something that isn’t real and a computer makes it), mission (when someone goes far away, and he has some work or task there). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A Black Hawk is a helicopter . Soldiers use it. Last week, the helicopter flies without pilots. It happens at Fort Campbell, US. There are two flights . One flight is 30 minutes long. The helicopter flies through a city. It is not a real city. A computer makes it. Then, the helicopter lands. The helicopter uses special technology. Shoppers in Beijing, China, lined up overnight in freezing temperatures for the chance to buy scarce Winter Olympics souvenirs, including stuffed versions of Olympics Games mascot panda Bing Dwen Dwen. On Monday, stores sold out of the pandas at many locations, including the Olympics facilities, where Chinese volunteers and foreign visitors had lined up for hours. Those who avoided the queue paid as much as 17 times the retail price on the outside market. Sellers sold stuffed toys there for over 500 dollars online. Police issued public warnings against buying the mascot from scalpers , and they punished three people for price gouging . Limited supplies were due to two reasons. The Games opening ceremony was during the middle of the Lunar New Year holiday, and many factories closed just before the demand suddenly increased for the Bing Dwen Dwen toys. Difficult words: scarce (not available in necessary amounts), scalper (a person who buys large amounts of something, and he sells it at a higher price), price goug e (to take advantage of high demand for something and charge high prices for it). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Difficult words: stuffed (a toy which has a soft filling inside), mascot (a person or thing which people use as a symbol of an event, and it brings good luck), demand (when many people want to buy the same thing). A convoy of trucks blocked Canada’s border with the US, and protesters refused to leave until the government ended all vaccine mandates and COVID-19 restrictions. Hundreds of trucks were in the demonstration to bring traffic to a standstill, and the event paralyzed the capital city of Ottawa. On Sunday, the city declared a state of emergency, and the Ottawa mayor said that the protests were out of control. Canada’s prime minister said that the protests had to stop, and he promised to send help. Residents were upset with the disruption, noise, and pollution, and many local businesses closed. Most of the protests were peaceful; however, some people reported vandalism and racial abuse. Despite being accused of being too careful, police arrested several people, and they took fuel cans and propane that kept the trucks running. Difficult words: mandate (an official rule or law that you have to do something), paralyze (to stop a system or place from working normally). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Police also arrested several drivers, but some people said that they could be more strict. The protests have been going on for over two weeks, and Canada’s prime minister offered to help the city. Difficult words: mandate (an official rule which says that people must do something), complain (to say that something is wrong), seize (to take something by force and keep it). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

China is showcasing low-carbon technologies for the green Winter Olympics; however, there’s strong criticism over the environmental impact of the Games. Beijing announced plans to run a carbon-negative Winter Games. It will use technologies such as natural refrigeration at ice rinks or venues powered by wind farms. According to officials, the Games are a driving force to improve the environment. China is the world’s biggest polluter, and it wants to show off its leadership in climate-friendly technology. However, environmentalists complained about the excessive use of artificial snow. For months, hundreds of snow generators created snow in arid mountains that receive little natural snow and have little water. Officials claimed the snow generators used the most advanced systems for international sustainability requirements. Difficult words: showcase (to show the best qualities or parts of something), arid (dry), sustainability (the idea that people can make goods and services should without damage to the environment, and therefore they can continue for a long time). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Difficult words: green (the idea to protect the environment), impact (how something affects something else), hydrogen (a light gas which does not harm the natural world as petrol or gas do). After coronavirus restrictions closed cinemas to the public, a Finnish chain of theaters named Finnkino came up with an alternative . The company is renting out screens to private groups and starting ‘Big screen gaming’. The event gives players a chance to rent an entire cinema for themselves and their friends. The maximum is a group of ten people, and the cost is about 280 dollars per group, which is about twice the price of a regular movie ticket. For that price, players get two and a half hours of uninterrupted gametime. All gamers need to do is bring their own consoles , games, and wireless controllers, and they can use the entire cinema to play their favorite games. Finnkino is offering the service in two theaters in the capital city of Helsinki, where it started on January 17. Later, the service could spread to other cities if there’s demand. Difficult words: alternative (another possibility or choice), console (a small electric device for playing video games), entire (whole). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

People need to bring their own consoles , games, and wireless controllers. They pay 280 dollars per group for a session which lasts two and a half hours. This is about twice as much as one person pays for a cinema ticket. Finnkino started to offer this service one month ago. If more people are interested, it could spread to other cities. Difficult words: rent out (to let someone use something, and he will pay money for it), console (a small electric device for playing video games), wireless (a device which works without a cable). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Dutch-owned trawler FV Martinis is the world’s second biggest fishing vessel, and it has shed more than 100,000 dead fish into the Atlantic Ocean off France. A fishing industry represented the vessel’s owner and explained that the spill was caused by a rupture in the net of the trawler. The fish mainly were blue whiting, a sub-species of cod that is used to mass- produce fish fingers, fish oil and meal. According to an environmental group Sea Shepherd, the spill covers an area of about 3,000 square meters. France’s maritime minister called the images shocking of the floating dead fish, and he asked to launch an investigation. Trawlers like the Martinis use drag nets more than a kilometer long, and they put the fish in onboard factories. Environmentalists heavily criticize this practice. They say that the nets catch all fish, which makes it difficult for the population to grow big again. It has an impact on the fish population and on the predators such as dolphins who starve as a result. Difficult words: trawler (a large boat that uses a wide net to catch fish), shed (to drop), rupture (the act when something breaks or bursts suddenly), mass- (a large amount). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

More than 100,000 dead fish went into the ocean off France, and the spill covered 3,000 square meters. Photos of the spill shocked France, and officials asked to investigate the situation. People who care about the environment often say that these big ships are very bad for fish. Wide nets catch too many fish, and they also catch other animals which live in the sea. Another problem is for the animals, which eat the fish because they have nothing to eat. Difficult words: spill (to flow out from a container), burst (to break open), investigate (to find out what happened). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The US national Wear Red Day is a campaign from the American Heart Association, to raise awareness about heart disease in women. On the first Friday of February, Americans wear red to show that heart disease kills one out of every three American women every year. Although heart disease is about 80% preventable , it is the number one killer of all women. In fact, heart disease kills more women than all cancers today. Risks for heart disease are high blood pressure, high levels of cholesterol , high body mass index , smoking, and genetics, or what conditions they get from their family. Experts are seeing an increase in heart disease in younger and younger women who they never thought were at risk. Heart disease takes a long time to develop, and people can prevent it by caring about their health. The best ways are to pay attention to what you eat and exercise regularly. Limit sugary drinks and eat more grains, fruits, and vegetables. Pay attention to your body and learn healthy ways to cope with stress. Difficult words: preventable (something that can be stopped from happening), cholesterol (a fat-like substance in all cells in the body), body mass index (a number that indicates high body fatness). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Many women in their 20s and 30s already have some kind of heart disease, which was unusual ten or twenty years ago. Heart disease is about 80% preventable, which means that people can often stop it from happening. The most important things are a healthy diet and enough exercise. People should eat enough grains, fruit and vegetables and drink less sugary drinks. More important things are to stop smoking, get enough sleep, and see friends. Difficult words: aware (knowing that something exists), cancer (a disease when a part of the body starts to grow without control), diet (the food which somebody eats). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Austria is the first country in Europe to pass a law that will require most adults to get vaccinated against COVID-19. The mandate to get vaccinated for residents aged 18 and over is the first of its kind in Europe. On Thursday, the mandate cleared its last legislative hurdle . The government’s house approved it, and the President signed the law on Friday. In mid-March, police will start to check people’s vaccination status during traffic stops and checks on coronavirus rules. People who can’t produce proof of vaccination will be asked in writing to do so, and they will get a fine of up to 600 euros. In the next part, officials will check the national vaccination database, and they will send reminders to unvaccinated people. They will give them dates to get vaccinated, and if they do not, they can get potential fines. At present, 69% of the country’s population is fully vaccinated, and the government is preparing to ease some coronavirus rules. Difficult words: mandate (an official order to do something), hurdle (a problem or difficulty that someone has to overcome), proof (a fact that shows that something exists or is true). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

People who do not show evidence of a vaccine can pay a fine of up to 600 euros. Later, officials will check information from the country’s list of vaccinations. They will see who did not get a vaccine, and this person will get a message with a date. On this date, the person must get the vaccine or he or she will pay a fine. Some people are very angry, because they do not want to have the vaccine, and they want to pay the fine. Difficult words: obligatory (something that a person has to do because it is a rule or law), evidence (a thing, document, or information which shows that something exists or it is true), fine (money which somebody has to pay when he breaks a rule or law). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Difficult words: law (an official rule for all people of a country), vaccine (a medicine that makes you stronger against a disease), fine (money which someone has to pay when he breaks an official rule).
